title: Merged excerpts are re-cut from the cues (R1000)
body:
Implements `docs/plans/oracle/recut-merged-excerpts.md` — **OD-4 / R1000**, evidence **BL-10**.

`merge_overlapping` concatenated the texts of two partially overlapping windows, so every character in the overlap was paid for once per window instead of once — and with many overlapping windows the concatenation compounded.

It now takes the video's transcript and **re-cuts** each merged span from the cues.

**The bound is a property, not an estimate.** Merged spans are disjoint and cue membership is decided on the cue's start alone, so each cue's text lands in at most one excerpt. `transcript_characters` is the same single-space join `_text_between` performs — a denominator omitting the separators would make the bound *false* — and it is also the denominator R28's saturation ratio needs, so the two documents cannot drift into two definitions.

**Merging on exact touch is kept** and must not be relaxed to a strict `<`: it is what makes surviving spans strictly disjoint, which is half the proof.

An excerpt from another video is now a `ValueError`, retiring the per-video grouping: the only caller passes one video's windows and R22 forbids holding a channel at once, so "never merge across videos" becomes *unaskable* rather than enforced.

**Measured on the real corpus, before and after:**

```
characters of excerpt text   232,728,580  ->  19,867,410   (11.7x)
bundles written                      650  ->         239
projected tokens              58,182,407  ->   4,967,112
data/bundles/ on disk              224 MB ->       20 MB
```

BL-10 measured 4.8x on a 33-minute review; the same defect on a 91-minute video here was **57x** — a 213,000-character transcript producing a 12,166,000-character excerpt. The projection is the one number the checkpoint exists to produce.

**The blind tests went furthest of any so far.** Their author wrote a reference implementation from the plan in a throwaway copy outside its worktree, confirmed its tests pass against that, confirmed the old concatenating merge turns **exactly** the R1000 tests red, and confirmed that relaxing the touch rule to `<` fails the two touch tests — the bound proved from both sides.

It exercises the bound as a seeded generated property over 16 seeds and four window-width regimes rather than one hand-built case, and it guards the marker-collision trap I hit while writing my own version (`cue1` being a substring of `cue10`) with its own test.

The regression uses a **synthetic** transcript of BL-10's measured geometry, because R21 holds the corpus local-only; BL-10's real figures are recorded as provenance and what is asserted is the bound.

1180 passing.
